summary: The candidate fixes all three reported paths when PyTorch's Metal memory APIs succeed, but its compatibility fallback restores uncapped host-memory reporting and its new registered test violates the repository CI taxonomy. This is a partial fix, not a complete resolution.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction across the SRT, MPS device-property, and multimodal production paths; observed 56 GiB available and 64 GiB total instead of 40/48 GiB.
Independent simulated Metal API integration through all three reported production paths; observed 40 GiB available and 48 GiB total.
Absent and raising Metal-limit APIs both returned uncapped 64 GiB total / 56 GiB available against a 48 GiB limit.
All applicable style checks passed, but check-registered-tests rejected MLX registration from a unit-test directory that permits only CPU suites.

gpu_execution.evidence: Prepared host is Linux/x86_64 with ROCm; torch.backends.mps.is_built() and is_available() were both false. AMD execution cannot validate Apple Metal accounting.

remaining_counterexamples: If torch.mps.recommended_max_memory is absent, the candidate reports host total/available memory and can exceed Metal's recommended working-set limit.
If torch.mps.recommended_max_memory raises or returns an invalid/non-positive value, the same unsafe host-memory fallback remains.
The candidate's registered regression file fails repository pre-commit taxonomy validation because a unit test registers an MLX CI suite.
remaining_limitations: No Apple Silicon or macOS device was available, so real MTLDevice values and UMA paging/stability were not measured.
No MPS serving workload or model execution was possible.
No native rebuild was applicable because the candidate is Python-only.
The image-prepared checkout matched the recorded base commit; origin/main had advanced to bd45cd5 during review but contained no overlapping fix for these MPS paths.
